title: A stack in an array
summary: The array stands upright like a container. numItems counts the items and is also the next free cell.

checkpoints.text: The stack is a `char` array of 10 cells and one int, `numItems`. It is 0: nothing is stored yet, so the next push goes into cell 0, at the bottom.
`A` was written into cell `numItems` (0), then `numItems` went up to 1. It now points at the empty cell above A.
A, B and C are stacked with C on top. `numItems` is 3: three items, and cell 3 is the next free one.
`top()` reads the cell just below `numItems`, which is C. Nothing moves: top only looks.
Pop does it in the other order: `--numItems` comes down to 2 first, then the C in cell 2 is returned.
D was pushed into cell 2. The old C was still in that cell, but it was no longer part of the stack, so D simply wrote over it.
Popped C, D, B, A: always the newest item first. `numItems` is back at 0, so the stack is empty. Push and pop each touch one cell and one int, so both are O(1).
